result.scope_note: The claim's timestamp (June 2022) and scope (worldwide) are taken as given; the protocol rule that HEAD responses omit body content is a persistent HTTP standard feature.

explanation.text: A HEAD response lacks a response body, per RFC 9112 section 3.2 and multiple RFC citations spanning 1999 to 2022.
RFC 9110, 9111, 9112 were published June 2022 and collectively define the HTTP standard, establishing HEAD response rules.
Span 449 from RFC 9112 explicitly states that any response to a HEAD request is always terminated by the first empty line after header fields and cannot contain a message body.
